question.prompt:
In the circle shown, \(M\) is the midpoint of arc \(\overset{\frown}{CAB},\) and segment \(MP\) is perpendicular to chord \(AB\) at \(P.\) If the measure of chord \(AC\) is \(x\) and that of segment \(AP\) is \(x+1,\) then segment \(PB\) has measure equal to:

[Figure 1](figures/1972_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Because \(M\) bisects the arc from \(C\) through \(A\) to \(B\), the arcs \(\overset{\frown}{CAM}\) and \(\overset{\frown}{MB}\) are equal. In particular, their chords satisfy \(MC=MB\). We will construct another segment equal to these chords so that the perpendicular \(MP\) becomes an altitude of an isosceles triangle.

[Figure 1](figures/1972_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)

Extend \(BA\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(D\) with \(AD=AC=x\). We claim that \(MD=MC\).

Let the common measure of arcs \(\overset{\frown}{CAM}\) and \(\overset{\frown}{MB}\) be \(\phi\) degrees. The inscribed angle theorem gives
\[
\angle MAB=\frac{\phi}{2}.
\]
The angle \(\angle CAM\) intercepts the other arc from \(C\) to \(M\), which does not contain \(A\), so
\[
\angle CAM=\frac{360^\circ-\phi}{2}
=180^\circ-\frac{\phi}{2}.
\]
Since \(AD\) is opposite to \(AB\), we also have
\[
\angle MAD=180^\circ-\angle MAB=\angle CAM.
\]
Thus triangles \(MAD\) and \(MAC\) are congruent by side-angle-side: they share \(AM\), have \(AD=AC\), and have equal included angles. Therefore \(MD=MC=MB\).

Triangle \(DMB\) is consequently isosceles. Since \(MP\perp DB\), its altitude from \(M\) bisects \(DB\), giving \(PD=PB\). The diagram places \(P\) between \(A\) and \(B\), so the points occur in the order \(D,A,P,B\). Hence
\[
PB=PD=DA+AP=x+(x+1)=\boxed{2x+1}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Extend the chord to build an isosceles triangle
